problem: Consider the surface ${2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}=2.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,-1,1),$ what is the value of $\frac{c}{b}?$

feedback.problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=xy$ along the polar curve $r=6$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
In polar coordinates, the formula for the line integral is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

 

The connection between polar and Cartesian coordinates gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

So, along our curve, we have $x=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $, where $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}.$

Now, since $f(x,y)=xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =36\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(6)=0,\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}36\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot 6\cdot \text{d}\theta  \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ $\text{d}u=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  & =6{\int }_{0}^{3\sqrt{3}}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}{|}_{0}^{3\sqrt{3}} \\  & =3({(3\sqrt{3})}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =3\cdot 27 \\  & =81\end{aligned}
$$
